items.title: A power of four
items.prose: Work without a calculator.
items.question: What is $\log_4 0.0625$?

feedback.generic: Write 0.0625 as a fraction, then as a power of 4.

byKey.pos: You gave the power for 16. A sixteenth is $4^{-2}$, so its power is negative.
byKey.places: You counted the four decimal places, as for base 10, or used base 2. In base 4, $\tfrac{1}{16} = 4^{-2}$.

explain.text: $0.0625 = \tfrac{1}{16} = \tfrac{1}{4^2} = 4^{-2}$. A logarithm asks for the power, so $\log_4 0.0625 = -2$. Numbers between 0 and 1 have negative logarithms.

items.title: Order tickets
items.prose: An order ticket names one of 5 shares, buy or sell, and an order type. There are 3 types: market, limit and stop.
items.question: How many different tickets are there?

feedback.correct: Five shares, two sides, three types: $5 \times 2 \times 3 = 30$.
feedback.generic: Each ticket makes three choices in a row. Multiply the number of options for each.

byKey.add: You added the options, 5 + 2 + 3. Each share goes with every side and every type, so they multiply.
byKey.side: You left out buy or sell. That doubles the 15 share and type pairs.

explain.text: Every share can pair with either side, and each pair with any of three types. Choices made one after another multiply: $5 \times 2 \times 3 = 30$.

items.title: Round the rim
items.prose: A pulley of radius 6 cm turns through 1.8 radians.
items.question: How far does a point on the rim travel, in cm?

feedback.generic: In radians, the arc is the radius times the angle.

byKey.divide: You divided the radius by the angle. Each radian adds one radius of arc, so multiply.
byKey.add: You added the radius and the angle. Each radian adds one radius of arc, so multiply.
byKey.degrees: You treated 1.8 as degrees. The angle is already in radians, so $s = r\theta$ needs no conversion.

explain.text: One radian sweeps an arc as long as the radius, 6 cm. So 1.8 radians sweep $1.8 \times 6 = 10.8$ cm. That is $s = r\theta$.

items.title: Two terms known
items.prose: A geometric sequence has 3rd term 12 and 6th term 96.
items.question: What is its 10th term?

feedback.generic: From term 3 to term 6 is 3 steps, so $r^3 = 96 / 12$.

byKey.power-n: You used $3 \times 2^{10}$. The first term has had no doublings, so term 10 has had 9.
byKey.first-term: You treated 12 as the first term. It is the 3rd, so term 10 is only 7 steps after it.
byKey.arith: You added 28 each step. The sequence is geometric, so each step multiplies by the same ratio.

explain.text: Three steps take 12 to 96, so $r^3 = 8$ and $r = 2$. Term 10 is 4 steps after term 6: $u_{10} = 96 \times 2^4 = 1536$. Check: $a = 3$ and $3 \times 2^9 = 1536$.

items.title: Four falls, four rises
items.prose: A share price falls 3% a day for 4 days, then rises 3% a day for the next 4 days.
items.question: Which gives the price now as a multiple of the starting price?

options.text: $1$, since the rises undo the falls
options.why: Each 3% rise is on a lower price than the falls started from. The pair $0.97 \times 1.03$ is 0.9991, below 1.
You applied the rise once. Each of the four rising days multiplies by 1.03.
You paired each fall with a rise, then counted eight pairs. Eight days make four pairs.

feedback.correct: Each day multiplies by its factor, and order does not matter: $(0.97 \times 1.03)^4 \approx 0.9964$.
feedback.generic: Turn each move into a factor, then multiply all eight.

explain.text: A 3% fall multiplies by 0.97 and a 3% rise by 1.03. Eight days multiply four of each: $(0.97 \times 1.03)^4 = 0.9991^4 \approx 0.9964$. The price ends about 0.36% lower, not back where it began.

items.title: Roots and reciprocals
items.prose: Work without a calculator.
items.question: What is $125^{2/3} \times 625^{-1/4}$?

feedback.generic: A denominator in the power is a root. A minus sign in the power is a reciprocal.

byKey.negative: You read $625^{-1/4}$ as −5. A negative power gives a reciprocal, not a negative number.
byKey.no-flip: You found the fourth root, 5, but kept it. The minus sign in the power turns it into $\tfrac15$.

explain.text: The cube root of 125 is 5, and squaring gives 25. The fourth root of 625 is 5, and the minus sign makes it $\tfrac15$. So $25 \times \tfrac15 = 5$.

items.title: How much more each week
items.prose: You save £20 in week 1. Each week after that you save a fixed amount more than the week before. After 30 weeks you have saved £2,775 in all.
items.question: How much more do you save each week than the week before, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Write the week 30 amount as $20 + 29d$. Then pair the first and last weeks.

byKey.steps: You took week 30 as $20 + 30d$. Week 30 is only 29 steps after week 1.
byKey.average: You used the average week, £92.50, as week 30. The average is half of week 1 plus week 30.
byKey.flat: You found how far the average week sits above week 1. Week 30 sits twice as far above, over 29 steps.

explain.text: Week 30 is $20 + 29d$, and pairing first with last gives 15 pairs: $15(40 + 29d) = 2775$. So $40 + 29d = 185$ and $d = 5$. Check: week 30 is £165, and $15 \times 185 = 2775$.

items.title: Two vans from one depot
items.prose: Two straight roads leave a depot at $120^\circ$ to each other. One van drives 3 km along one road; a second drives 5 km along the other. Work without a calculator.
items.question: How far apart are the vans, in km?

feedback.correct: $c^2 = 9 + 25 + 15 = 49$, so the vans are 7 km apart.
feedback.generic: Use the cosine rule with the angle between the two known sides. Cosine is negative past 90°.

byKey.pythag: You used Pythagoras, $\sqrt{34}$. That needs a right angle; here the angle is $120^\circ$.
byKey.acute: You used $\cos 120^\circ = \tfrac12$. Past 90° cosine is negative: $\cos 120^\circ = -\tfrac12$.

explain.text: The cosine rule gives $c^2 = 3^2 + 5^2 - 2 \times 3 \times 5 \cos 120^\circ$. With $\cos 120^\circ = -\tfrac12$ this is $34 + 15 = 49$. So $c = 7$.

items.title: A roof truss
items.prose: A roof truss is a triangle. Its base is 10 m, and its two sloping sides are 7 m each. You may use a calculator.
items.question: What angle does each sloping side make with the base, in degrees to one decimal place?

feedback.correct: Half the base is 5 m, so $\cos\theta = \tfrac57$ and $\theta \approx 44.4^\circ$.
feedback.generic: Split the triangle down the middle into two right-angled triangles. Each has a base of 5 m.

byKey.apex: You found the angle at the top. The question asks for the angle at the base.
byKey.vertical: You used $\sin\theta = \tfrac57$, which gives the angle with the vertical. At the base, 5 m is the adjacent side.
byKey.radians: Your calculator is in radians. Switch it to degrees.

explain.text: The line from the top to the middle of the base splits the truss into two right-angled triangles. Each has hypotenuse 7 and adjacent side 5, so $\cos\theta = \tfrac57$. That gives $\theta \approx 44.4^\circ$.

items.title: Below £5,000
items.prose: A car worth £18,000 loses 12% of its value each year. You may use a calculator.
items.question: After how many whole years is it first worth less than £5,000?

feedback.correct: $n = \log(5/18) / \log 0.88 \approx 10.02$, so the value drops below £5,000 in year 11.
feedback.generic: Solve $18000 \times 0.88^n = 5000$ with logs, then check the whole years either side.

byKey.floor: You rounded 10.02 down. After 10 years the car is still worth £5,013.02.
byKey.simple: You took off £2,160 a year. Each year’s 12% is of a smaller value, so the fall slows.

explain.text: Dividing by 18,000 gives $0.88^n = \tfrac{5}{18}$, so $n = \dfrac{\log(5/18)}{\log 0.88} \approx 10.02$. After 10 years the car is worth £5,013.02, just above. After 11 it is £4,411.46.

items.title: Growing all the time
items.prose: £2,000 grows at a continuous rate of 5% a year for 2 years, then at a continuous 3% a year for 3 more years. You may use a calculator.
items.question: What is it worth then, to the nearest penny?

feedback.generic: Grow it for each stage with $e^{rt}$. The two factors multiply.

byKey.average: You used 4% for all 5 years. The 5% lasts 2 years and the 3% lasts 3, so weight by time: $0.10 + 0.09$.
byKey.annual: You added each rate once a year, $1.05^2 \times 1.03^3$. A continuous rate compounds all the time: use $e^{rt}$.
byKey.simple: You added 19% of £2,000. Continuous growth compounds, so use $e^{0.19}$.

explain.text: The first stage multiplies by $e^{0.05 \times 2} = e^{0.10}$, the second by $e^{0.03 \times 3} = e^{0.09}$. Powers of $e$ add, so the total factor is $e^{0.19}$. That gives $2000e^{0.19} \approx$ £2,418.50.

items.title: A daily cycle
items.prose: A desk’s message rate rises and falls through the day. The graph shows it, in thousands a minute, against hours after midnight.
items.question: Which equation fits the graph?

options.why: That wave rises first from the midline. This graph falls first, so $a$ is negative.
You took the trough-to-peak height, 6, as the amplitude. The amplitude is half of it.
That wave repeats every 24 hours. The graph repeats every 12.

feedback.correct: Midline 5, amplitude 3, falling first, period 12 hours: $a = -3$ and $b = \pi/6$.
feedback.generic: Read the midline, the amplitude, the time for one cycle and which way the graph leaves the midline.

explain.text: The graph runs between 2 and 8, so the midline is 5 and the amplitude 3. It leaves the midline going down, so $a = -3$. Troughs at 3 and 15 hours put the period at 12, so $b = 2\pi / 12 = \pi / 6$.

items.title: A sum that starts late
items.prose: Work without a calculator.
items.question: What is $\displaystyle\sum_{k=5}^{20} (3k + 2)$?

feedback.generic: Count the terms from $k = 5$ to $k = 20$, then find the first and last.

byKey.count: You counted $20 - 5 = 15$ terms. Both ends are included, so there are 16.
byKey.from-one: You started at $k = 1$. This sum starts at $k = 5$, so 5, 8, 11 and 14 are left out.

explain.text: There are $20 - 5 + 1 = 16$ terms, from 17 up to 62. Pairing first with last gives 8 pairs of 79, so the sum is 632. Check: from $k = 1$ the sum is 670, and $5 + 8 + 11 + 14 = 38$.

items.title: Sitting together
items.prose: Six traders sit in a row of six desks. Priya and Tom must sit next to each other. Sam must not sit at either end.
items.question: How many seatings are there?

feedback.correct: 240 seatings keep Priya and Tom together, and 96 of those put Sam at an end: $240 - 96 = 144$.
feedback.generic: Count the seatings with the pair together, then take away those with Sam at an end.

byKey.no-sam: You kept Priya and Tom together but let Sam sit anywhere. Take away the seatings with Sam at an end.
byKey.one-end: You took away Sam at the left end only. Sam at the right end is another 48.
byKey.no-swap: You kept Priya on Tom’s left. The pair can sit either way round, which doubles the count.

explain.text: With the pair glued, 5 blocks give $5! \times 2 = 240$ seatings. With Sam fixed at one end, 4 blocks give $4! \times 2 = 48$, so 96 for both ends. That leaves $240 - 96 = 144$.

items.title: Every solution
items.prose: Solve $\cos 3x = \tfrac12$ for $0^\circ \le x < 180^\circ$.
items.question: Select all that apply: which values of $x$ are solutions?

options.why: You used $180^\circ - 60^\circ$ for $3x$, as for sine. Cosine is $-\tfrac12$ at $120^\circ$.
You solved $\cos x = \tfrac12$. At $x = 60^\circ$, $3x = 180^\circ$, where cosine is $-1$.
You added $360^\circ$ to $120^\circ$. Cosine is $-\tfrac12$ at both.

feedback.generic: Let $u = 3x$. Since $x$ runs up to 180°, $u$ runs up to 540°.

explain.text: Put $u = 3x$, so $u$ runs from 0° to 540°. $\cos u = \tfrac12$ at 60°, 300° and 420°; the next, 660°, is past 540°. Dividing by 3 gives 20°, 100° and 140°.

items.title: A missing constant
items.prose: In the expansion of $(1 + ax)^6$, the coefficient of $x^2$ is 135, and $a > 0$.
items.question: What is $a$?

feedback.generic: Write the $x^2$ term as $\binom62 (ax)^2$, then solve for $a$.

byKey.square: You stopped at 9, or forgot to square $a$. The term holds $(ax)^2 = a^2x^2$, so $a^2 = 9$.
byKey.six: You used 6 as the coefficient. Choosing 2 brackets from 6 gives $\binom62 = 15$.

explain.text: The $x^2$ term picks $ax$ from 2 of the 6 brackets: $\binom62 (ax)^2 = 15a^2x^2$. So $15a^2 = 135$, $a^2 = 9$ and $a = 3$, since $a > 0$.

items.title: Two tech shares
items.prose: A watchlist holds 12 shares, 5 of them tech. You pick 4 at random, every set of 4 equally likely.
items.question: What is the chance that exactly 2 are tech? Give a decimal to three places.

feedback.generic: Count the sets with 2 tech and 2 others, then divide by all sets of 4.

byKey.other: You counted the tech pairs but not the other two shares. Each tech pair goes with any of the 21 pairs of others.
byKey.replace: You treated the picks as independent, with 5/12 each time. Picking without putting back changes the odds.
byKey.one-order: You counted one order: tech, tech, other, other. There are $\binom42 = 6$ orders of two tech and two others.

explain.text: There are $\binom{12}{4} = 495$ sets of 4. Two tech from 5 is $\binom52 = 10$ ways and two others from 7 is $\binom72 = 21$. That gives $210/495 \approx 0.424$.

items.title: There and back
items.prose: A share’s log return on Monday is 0.05. On Tuesday it closes back at Monday’s opening price. You may use a calculator.
items.question: What is Tuesday’s simple return, as a decimal to four places?

feedback.generic: Two log returns that bring the price back must add to 0. Then turn Tuesday’s back into a simple return.

byKey.log: You stopped at Tuesday’s log return. Turn it back with $e^{x} - 1$.
byKey.flip: You flipped Monday’s simple return, $e^{0.05} - 1 = 0.0513$. A rise and a fall of the same size do not cancel.
byKey.sign: Tuesday's log return is −0.05, so e^(−0.05) − 1 is below zero. A positive 0.0488 books the fall as a gain.

explain.text: Log returns add, and the two days end where they began, so Tuesday’s is $-0.05$. Its simple return is $e^{-0.05} - 1 \approx -0.0488$. Monday’s simple return was $+0.0513$, so the fall is the smaller percentage.

items.title: Length of a combination
items.prose: $\mathbf{u} = (3, -1)$ and $\mathbf{v} = (2, 4)$.
items.question: What is $|2\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{v}|$? Give two decimal places.

feedback.generic: Build the vector first, component by component, then use Pythagoras.

byKey.mags: You worked out $2|\mathbf{u}| - |\mathbf{v}|$. Lengths do not subtract; build the vector first.
byKey.plus: You added $\mathbf{v}$. The question takes it away.
byKey.abs-sum: You added the sizes of the parts, 4 and 6. A length uses Pythagoras: $\sqrt{4^2 + 6^2}$.

explain.text: $2\mathbf{u} = (6, -2)$, and subtracting $\mathbf{v}$ gives $(4, -6)$. Its length is $\sqrt{16 + 36} = \sqrt{52} \approx 7.21$. Lengths do not subtract: $2|\mathbf{u}| - |\mathbf{v}|$ is only 1.85.

items.title: Signs from the quadrant
items.prose: An angle $\theta$ lies between $180^\circ$ and $270^\circ$, and $\tan\theta = \tfrac{15}{8}$.
items.question: What is $\cos\theta - \sin\theta$? Give a decimal to four places.

feedback.generic: Draw a right-angled triangle with sides 8 and 15. Then choose each sign from the quadrant.

byKey.sign: You took both as positive. Between 180° and 270° the point is left of and below the centre, so both are negative.
byKey.second: You made only cosine negative. Below the axis, sine is negative too.
byKey.fourth: You made only sine negative. Left of the axis, cosine is negative too.

explain.text: $\tan\theta = \tfrac{15}{8}$ gives a triangle with sides 8, 15 and $\sqrt{64 + 225} = 17$. Between 180° and 270° both are negative: $\cos\theta = -\tfrac{8}{17}$ and $\sin\theta = -\tfrac{15}{17}$. So $\cos\theta - \sin\theta = \tfrac{7}{17} \approx 0.4118$.

items.title: A difference of logs
items.prose: Work without a calculator.
items.question: Solve $\log_3 (x + 6) - \log_3 x = 2$.

feedback.generic: Combine the two logs into one with the quotient law, then undo the log.

byKey.cube: You used $2^3 = 8$. Undoing $\log_3$ of a number equal to 2 gives $3^2 = 9$.
byKey.double: You used $3 \times 2 = 6$. Undoing the log raises 3 to the power 2, which is 9.

explain.text: The quotient law gives $\log_3 \tfrac{x + 6}{x} = 2$, so $\tfrac{x + 6}{x} = 3^2 = 9$. Then $x + 6 = 9x$ and $x = \tfrac68 = 0.75$. Check: $\log_3 6.75 - \log_3 0.75 = \log_3 9 = 2$.

items.title: Paid today and every year
items.prose: A fund pays £60 today and £60 on the same date every year after, forever. Money is discounted at 4% a year.
items.question: What is the whole stream worth today, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Write the values as a geometric series with ratio $\tfrac{1}{1.04}$, starting with today’s £60.

byKey.today: You valued the payments from next year on. Today’s £60 is worth £60 and must be added.
byKey.minus: You took today’s £60 away. It is paid now, so it adds to the value.
byKey.ratio: You used 0.04 as the ratio. Each year’s value is the last one divided by 1.04.

explain.text: The values are $60 + \tfrac{60}{1.04} + \tfrac{60}{1.04^2} + \dots$, a geometric series with $r = \tfrac{1}{1.04}$. Its sum to infinity is $\dfrac{60}{1 - 1/1.04} = \dfrac{60 \times 1.04}{0.04} = 1560$. That is today’s £60 plus £1,500 for the rest.

items.title: A third of the way
items.prose: $\overrightarrow{OA} = \mathbf{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{OB} = \mathbf{b}$. X lies on AB with $AX : XB = 1 : 2$.
items.question: Which vector is $\overrightarrow{OX}$?

options.why: You measured the third from B. X is a third of the way from A, so it sits nearer A.
You wrote $\overrightarrow{AB}$ as $\mathbf{a} - \mathbf{b}$. A vector from A to B is end minus start: $\mathbf{b} - \mathbf{a}$.
You took a third of $\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b}$. That point is on the line from O to the parallelogram’s far corner, not on AB.

feedback.generic: Go from O to A, then a third of the way along $\overrightarrow{AB}$.

explain.text: $\overrightarrow{AB} = \mathbf{b} - \mathbf{a}$, and X is a third of the way along it. So $\overrightarrow{OX} = \mathbf{a} + \tfrac13(\mathbf{b} - \mathbf{a})$. Collecting terms gives $\tfrac23\mathbf{a} + \tfrac13\mathbf{b}$.

items.title: Codes with a letter
items.prose: A broker’s account code has 4 characters. Each is a digit from 0 to 9 or a letter from A to F.
items.question: How many codes have four different characters and at least one letter?

feedback.correct: Codes with four different characters, minus those using digits only: $43680 - 5040 = 38640$.
feedback.generic: Count the codes with four different characters. Then take away the ones with no letter.

byKey.distinct: You counted every code with four different characters. Those made of digits alone have no letter.
byKey.repeat-ok: You allowed repeats. Every character must differ, so count ordered picks without putting back.
byKey.total-minus: You took the digit-only codes from all $16^4$ codes. The rest still include codes with repeats.

explain.text: Four different characters from 16 give $16 \times 15 \times 14 \times 13 = 43680$ codes. Of those, $10 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7 = 5040$ use digits only. The other 38640 hold at least one letter.

items.title: When two accounts meet
items.prose: Account A holds £1,000 growing at a continuous 5% a year. Account B holds £1,200 growing at a continuous 3% a year. You may use a calculator.
items.question: After how many years are they worth the same? Give two decimal places.

feedback.generic: Set $1000e^{0.05t} = 1200e^{0.03t}$ and gather the exponentials on one side.

byKey.add: You added the rates. Dividing $e^{0.05t}$ by $e^{0.03t}$ subtracts the powers, leaving $e^{0.02t}$.
byKey.simple: You grew each account by a fixed amount a year. Continuous growth compounds, so use $e^{rt}$.

explain.text: Dividing both sides by $1000e^{0.03t}$ gives $e^{0.02t} = 1.2$. Taking $\ln$: $0.02t = \ln 1.2 \approx 0.1823$, so $t \approx 9.12$ years. Each account is then worth about £1,577.

items.title: Paying from today
items.prose: You borrow £10,000 today and repay it with 10 equal yearly payments. The first payment is today. Interest is 5% a year. You may use a calculator.
items.question: What is each payment, to the nearest penny?

feedback.correct: The ten payments’ values today must add to £10,000: $P = \dfrac{500}{1.05\,(1 - 1.05^{-10})} \approx$ £1,233.38.
feedback.generic: Value each payment today, the first at full value, and add them as a geometric series. Set the total to £10,000.

byKey.end: You paid at the end of each year. The first payment is today, so each one is a year earlier.
byKey.no-interest: You split £10,000 into ten parts. That ignores the interest on what is still owed.
byKey.simple: You charged 5% of £10,000 every year. The balance falls as you pay, so the interest falls too.
byKey.future: You grew the whole loan for 10 years, then split it. Early payments cut the balance, so less interest builds up.

explain.text: Payment $k$, counting today’s as 0, is worth $P / 1.05^k$, so the ten add to $P \cdot \dfrac{1 - 1.05^{-10}}{1 - 1/1.05}$. Setting this to 10000 gives $P \approx 1233.38$. That is £1,295.05, the end-of-year payment, divided by 1.05.
